The promise of AI and MCP is that integrating the physical and digital worlds is easier than ever. That may be true, but data siloes and real world messiness still stymy projects. Rather than wait for a perfect data environment, leading companies are building incremental progress, uniting inspection data from autonomous robots with other information sources to help identify problems, make better decisions, and act on insights more quickly.

We are thrilled to expand our collaboration with @GlobalFoundries. In addition to deploying Spot across their global manufacturing network, GF will be the first semiconductor manufacturer to test humanoid robots as part of Atlas early adopter program.

GF has worked with Boston Dynamics and Spot for over four years and recently expanded the program to Singapore, where two Spot robots have traveled nearly 900 kilometers and completed more than 90,000 inspections in sub-fab areas since April, achieving a 99% mission success rate.

When rubber meets the road, we have to get creative to ensure our robots will be reliable and performant outside of the lab! Putting wheels on Atlas let us test how faithfully an RL whole-body controller can work with real actuators running at the edge.

AGIBOT G2: The 24-Hour Nonstop Convenience Store Challenge

Working nonstop for 24 hours, powering through four grueling shifts, and completing hundreds of real-world service tasks. 

In this "no-holds-barred" public evaluation, AGIBOT G2 not only withstood the pressure of real customer traffic but also demonstrated incredible stability. 

Let’s look back at the highlights of these 24 hours and check out G2's "Work Performance Report"! 👇

AGIBOT G2 Max: A heavy-duty industrial robot built for demanding manufacturing and logistics tasks.  

With 21 degrees of freedom, up to 40 kg of dual-arm handling capacity, and an adjustable working height from 0.1 to 2.5 meters, G2 Max combines force-controlled manipulation, omnidirectional mobility and multiple safety features to support demanding industrial operations.  

From production lines and CNC machine tending to warehouse handling and pallet operations, the G2 family is bringing robotic capabilities into real industrial workflows.  Built for the demands of real work.
